claim: Library size: the abstract states 315 lipids
locus_a: Article abstract (not held; count supplied in the curation brief): 315 FILs
locus_b: SI: 74 distinct FILs. 42 numbered synthesis headings in section 3.2 + 32 SP members named only in figure captions S20-S26/S38-S44 and on the Figure S48-S51 x-axes; Figure S51 draws 75 ticks = SM102 + 74 FILs (measured, pitch CV 0.028); the strings '315', 'library', 'combinatorial', 'total of' and 'screen' occur 0 times in the 100-page SI
what_we_emitted: 74 FILs enumerated; the abstract's 315 is NOT reconciled and NOT assumed away
why: The SI is self-consistent at 74 across four independent loci (synthesis headings, NMR captions, MS captions, drawn axis labels). 315 cannot be checked without the article text. DECISIONS.md D-1.

locus_a: SI 3.2.1.2 sentence: 'The 3-(4-((6-bromohexanoyl)oxy)butoxy)propanoic acid was used' -- an ETHER-containing acid, which is the O-series material
locus_b: SI 3.2.1.2's own printed formula C42H80FNO7 (7 oxygens, no ether) AND the reaction scheme drawn directly beneath that heading on SI PDF p.25, which shows a plain C4 diester with no ether oxygen (read at 7x from the native 1153x107 raster)
why: Two loci against one sentence, and the two include the drawing. An ether would make the formula ...NO8; it is printed NO7.

locus_a: SI 3.2.1.3 sentence: 'The 5-(4-fluorobutoxy)-5-oxopentyl 6-bromohexanoate was used' -- a C4 linker, i.e. SSC4F1's material
locus_b: SI 3.2.1.3's printed formula C43H82FNO7 = the C5 member; and the F3 sub-series names its materials consistently (3.2.1.11 SSC5F3 cites '6-oxo-6-(4,4,4-trifluorobutoxy)hexyl 6-bromohexanoate', a C5 linker)
why: The reagent sentences at 3.2.1.2 and 3.2.1.3 are shifted by one position; the formulas and the parallel F3/F5/F7 sub-series are not. Series pattern + formula pin it, as with the 4A3-SC6 patch (CLAUDE.md s9, 2026-10-28).

locus_b: Figure S18 caption, Figure S36 caption, and the Figure S48-S51 x-axis labels all read 'SSCOF1'
why: One locus against three, and the three include a drawn axis label. No SSCO4 linker exists anywhere else in the paper.

locus_a: Heading reads 'SSC4F3'; its body reads 'The synthesis method for SSCF3 was similar...'
locus_b: SI 3.2.1.10's heading ALSO reads 'SSC4F3'; 3.2.1.9's printed formula C41H76F3NO7 and its material '4-oxo-4-(4,4,4-trifluorobutoxy)butyl 6-bromohexanoate' are both the C3 member, and SSC3F3 is otherwise missing from section 3.2 while appearing in Figure S13 and on the S48-S51 axes
why: Two headings cannot name one compound; the formula, the material and the roster all say the first is the C3 member.

locus_a: SI 3.2.2: '2-Heptyldecan-1-ol was used as the starting material' (C17)
locus_b: SI Materials p.3 lists '2-heptylnonan-1-ol (97%)' and NOT 2-heptyldecan-1-ol; SI 3.1.47's heading names the product '2-heptylnonyl 8-((2-hydroxyethyl)amino)octanoate'; its body charges '2-heptylnonan-1-ol (4.8 g, 20.0 mmol)'; its stated product is named the same way (C16)
what_we_emitted: 2-heptylnonyl. All 32 SP rows carry confidence = low and structure_assumed = 1
why: Three loci against one, and 2-heptyldecan-1-ol appears nowhere else in the paper. BUT no SP member has a formula or an m/z anywhere in the SI, so nothing in the paper measures the difference -- and the two differ by one CH2, which would make every SP lipid an ISOMER of its SS counterpart rather than one CH2 lighter. DECISIONS.md D-2.

claim: The P-series linker contains a benzylic CH2
locus_a: SI's printed formulas C46H80FNO8 / C46H78F3NO8 / C46H76F5NO8 / C46H74F7NO8 and the printed [M+H]+ for PF3/PF5/PF7, which agree with EACH OTHER to <=0.02 Da and sit exactly one CH2 (14.016 Da) below a benzyl-containing structure
locus_b: SI 3.2.1.8/16/24/32 reagent name '4-(3-(fluoroalkoxy)-3-oxopropoxy)BENZYL 6-bromohexanoate'; the intermediate on SI p.11 named '3-(4-(((6-bromohexanoyl)oxy)METHYL)phenoxy)propanoic acid' with 1H NMR 5.04 (s, 2H); SSCPF1's own 1H NMR 5.09-4.99 (m, 2H) and SSCPF5's 5.04 (s, 2H); Materials p.3 lists '4-hydroxybenzyl alcohol'
what_we_emitted: The benzyl-containing structure (C47...). All 8 P-series rows carry confidence = low and structure_assumed = 1
why: Four loci against a mutually-derived pair. A para-phenyl ester with no CH2 would give the printed C46 but would have no 2H singlet near 5.0 ppm, and 4-hydroxybenzyl alcohol would not be on the reagent list. NOT applied as a correction to the paper -- DECISIONS.md D-3.

locus_a: SI 3.2.1.30 prints C45H80F7NO7 and [M+H]+ 880.59, which agree with each other to 0.001 Da
locus_b: Its own reagent sentence names '2,2,3,3,4,4,4-Heptafluorobutyl 5-((6-bromohexanoyl)oxy)NONANOATE' (C9 -> C46), and its three series-mates SSCB4F1 (C46H88FNO7), SSCB4F3 (C46H86F3NO7) and SSCB4F5 (C46H84F5NO7) are all C46 and all match our build exactly
what_we_emitted: C46H82F7NO7; row carries confidence = low and structure_assumed = 1
why: A self-consistent HRMS pair against the reagent name plus three matching series-mates. Same shape as the P series. DECISIONS.md D-3.

locus_b: The same sentence's formula C42H74F7NO7 has monoisotopic [M+H]+ 838.5426, which equals our built structure to 4 decimal places
what_we_emitted: The structure implied by the formula (C42H74F7NO7)
why: The printed m/z disagrees with the printed formula by 17.3 Da. Where the two disagree, the HRMS line is not evidence; the formula here matches the series and the reagent name.

locus_b: The same sentence prints [M+H]+ 852.55, which equals our C43H76F7NO7 structure to 0.008 Da, and the C5 position in every other sub-series is C43
why: The printed formula is one carbon short of its own printed mass; the mass agrees with the series.

locus_b: The same sentence prints [M+H]+ 844.60, which equals our C45H82F5NO7 to 0.008 Da; every other FIL in the library has 7 or 8 oxygens
why: A dropped subscript. The printed mass settles it.

locus_b: The same sentence's formula C44H78F7NO7 equals our build exactly and has [M+H]+ 866.5739; 852.55 is the number printed for SSC5F7 four paragraphs earlier, and 3.2.1.29's entire 1H NMR integral list is a verbatim duplicate of 3.2.1.21 (SSCB2F5)
what_we_emitted: The structure implied by the formula (C44H78F7NO7)
why: The paragraph is a copy-paste; its formula was updated and its m/z and NMR were not.

locus_b: The same sentence prints [M+H]+ 882.62; our build from its own reagent name and its series position is C44H78F7NO8, [M+H]+ 882.5688
why: Both printed values are internally inconsistent (62 Da apart), so neither is evidence. The structure rests on the reagent sentence plus the O-series pattern (SSCOF1/F3/F5 are all ...NO8 and all match).

locus_a: SI 3.1.49 body charges 'TWO carboxylic acids -- 2-Hexyldecanoic acid (5.9 g, 23.0 mmol), 2-heptylnonanoic acid (3.6 g, 20.0 mmol)' and no alcohol
locus_b: Its own heading and its stated product are '6-((4-hydroxybutyl)amino)hexyl 2-heptylnonanoate'; SI 3.1.48 is the same paragraph with '2-Hexyldecanoic acid (5.9 g, 23.0 mmol), 6-bromohexan-1-ol (3.6 g, 20.0 mmol)'
what_we_emitted: AS core = 2-heptylnonanoic acid esterified to 6-bromohexan-1-ol, then aminated with 4-aminobutan-1-ol
why: 3.1.49's reagent line is 3.1.48's with the alcohol slot overwritten; an esterification of two acids is not a reaction. The heading, the product name and the AS/AL formula identity (both C41H76F3NO7 for ALC4F3/ASC4F3) all agree.

locus_a: SI 3.1.47 and 3.1.48 both charge the bromo-ester as '(2.0 g, 2.18 mmol)', implying MW 917 Da
locus_b: 6-bromohexyl 2-heptylnonanoate is C23H45BrO2, MW 433.5 -- 2.0 g is 4.61 mmol, not 2.18
what_we_emitted: nothing (no structure or value depends on it)
why: Recorded as further evidence that section 3.1-3.2 paragraphs were copied and partially updated, which is the mechanism behind the ten HRMS contradictions above.
